transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-31
Time: 10:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Aisha Khan (Redwood SE), Maya Li (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (CTO, Mistral Tech), Priya Singh (Head of MLOps, Mistral), Carlos Mendez (SRE, Mistral), Sofia Alvarez (Product, Mistral)

Summary:
Quarterly business review covering usage trends, unit costs, latency/reliability incidents, roadmap alignment (dedicated capacity and private deployment), and next steps for a pilot to reduce per-token costs.

Topics:
- Usage & cost trends (Q4)
- Reliability: incidents and SLOs
- Redwood Dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs
- Roadmap alignment and upcoming features (autoscaling policies, better batching)
- Security/doc requests and audit materials

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy new year early, uh we wanted to do a quick qbr and make sure we're aligned on usage and next steps. hey Liam, can you start with a quick state of where you are?
[00:18] Liam: Yeah thanks Jordan, um appreciate it. Overall things look good. We saw a big uptick in November when marketing pushed a new feature; tokens spiked about 42% month over month. Cost is up, obviously. We're seeing tail latency occasionally hit 800-900 ms on the chat endpoint during peak, which is creeping toward our acceptable limit.
[00:42] Aisha: Quick clarifying question - is that p95 or p99 you're calling 800-900ms?
[00:48] Liam: That's p99, sorry should have said that. p95 is closer to 260.
[00:53] Aisha: Got it. That helps.
[00:55] Priya: We're running the hosted endpoint for production and a small dedicated pool for some internal experiments. The dedicated is stable but not fully sized, we're planning capacity increases in Jan.
[01:10] Jordan: Thanks. On the cost side, Maya, did you pull the Q4 breakdown?
[01:14] Maya: Yep. High level: November spike pushed Q4 total tokens to ~1.8B tokens, with November being 800M. Average cost per 1k tokens for hosted models has been roughly $0.85 after discounts; dedicated unit economics look better once you hit about 200M tokens / month, but that's also dependent on utilization and model variant.
[01:36] Carlos: That's the nub - our utilization is only about 62% on the dedicated pool; we can't justify full reserved capacity at current usage. We need better autoscale or burst policies.
[01:48] Aisha: Good note. We recently rolled out a burst capacity option and new autoscale signals - we can tune the cooldowns and target utilization. For your workload pattern (spiky daily loads), a mixed approach of hosted + small dedicated pool with burst to hosted or to a lower-cost quantized variant often hits both cost and latency targets.
[02:09] Priya: The tradeoff I worry about is data residency and auditability. Some of our legal folks want logs retained for 12 months and a private VPC.
[02:19] Maya: We can definitely provide the audit logs and SOC2 reports. For VPC/private deployment - that is part of Redwood Private, which is a separate engagement. We have an enterprise package and on-prem options.
[02:31] Jordan: Also, just to flag, we've seen a couple of incidents - I think Carlos you logged two in Dec? Can you walk us through what happened and any mitigations you put in place?
[02:41] Carlos: Yeah on Dec 12 we had degraded throughput after a model update; latency spiked as KV cache warmed. It recovered after rolling back to the previous model variant. We also had a small networking hiccup on Dec 28 where one AZ had packet drops and requests were routed to a colder pool which introduced latency. We've added extra health checks and some fallback rules to route to a different region earlier.
[03:08] Aisha: The KV cache warming is something we can help with - we have a pre-warm technique and also can suggest prompt prefix caching for common flows. That usually brings down warm-up latency.
[03:20] Sofia: For roadmap alignment, we care about better deterministic latency at p99 and cost predictability. Any upcoming features that will help?
[03:30] Aisha: On the roadmap, in Q1 we're shipping improved batching heuristics and more aggressive prefix caching. There's also a tuning UI in Console to preview batching settings by route. That should improve efficiency and lower per-token cost for conversational flows.
[03:45] Jordan: We're also adding more quantization profiles and kernel selection improvements which help lower cost with minimal quality regression; we'll share recommended profiles for your models.
[03:53] Priya: That would be super helpful. We run a lot of retrieval-augmented prompts and want to avoid hallucination regressions when using quantized variants.
[04:03] Aisha: Totally - we'll include quality guardrails and suggested eval prompts to watch for.
[04:10] Liam: On the dedicated capacity note: what's the break-even again for reserved vs hosted? You mentioned 200M tokens a month but what's the assumed latency target?
[04:21] Jordan: Good question - the break-even assumes ~99% utilization and a p99 latency target under 350ms on the same model variant (non-quantized). If you can accept slightly higher p99 or use a quantized flavor, the break-even moves lower. We can run a custom econ model for your numbers.
[04:36] Maya: That's on my to-do list - I'll put together the break-even analysis for your exact November-December usage and model mix.
[04:44] Carlos: Also asking about security: our security team needs to see KMS integration details and key rotation.
[04:51] Maya: We'll toss the KMS architecture doc and rotation cadence into the doc packet.
[04:55] Jordan: Aisha, can we also do a throughput bench for their 8k token use-case? They mentioned long contexts for some agents.
[05:02] Aisha: Yes we can. We'll spin up a dedicated benchmark that mimics 8k streaming contexts and measure tokens/sec and p99. Expect raw results plus logs.
[05:12] Priya: Awesome. For timeline, we want to decide on a pilot resizing by mid-Jan. If dedicated sizing works, we may sign a reserve for Q2.
[05:22] Jordan: Makes sense. We'll aim to get the benchmark and econ analysis to you before Jan 10 so you can decide.
[05:28] Sofia: Any competitive intel that matters for us? We evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI earlier but costs at that scale were different.
[05:35] Jordan: Right - Anthropic had some strengths on instruction tuning and safety, OpenAI had a lot of product polish but cost and closed model constraints were concerns. For Redwood we focus on predictable infra and the hybrid hosting model.
[05:48] Liam: One nit - the Console's cost breakdown is great but we need more token-level tagging by feature so product owners can see which features are driving cost.
[05:58] Maya: We can enable route-level tags and share a guide on tagging events; that will let you break down cost per feature.
[06:07] Carlos: Ok that's helpful.
[06:10] Jordan: Quick recap - action items: Maya share Q4 usage/cost breakdown and SOC2/audit docs by Jan 3-5; Aisha run the 8k throughput benchmark and share results by Jan 10; Jordan will share a draft econ model; Priya to share growth forecast by Jan 4. Any objections?
[06:30] Priya: No objections, sounds good.
[06:32] Liam: No objections.
[06:34] Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the follow-on deep dive and I'll attach the ROI/break-even spreadsheet. Happy new year and talk soon.

End of transcript.
